PA.name: Personal Attack
PA.explanation: Attacking the character, traits, or circumstances of a speaker instead of addressing their argument.

TUQ.name: Who Are You to Talk? (Tu Quoque)
TUQ.explanation: Rejecting an argument by pointing out that the speaker does not follow their own advice or principles.

AH.name: Ad Hominem
AH.explanation: Dismissing an argument based on the speaker’s identity, group membership, or personal attributes rather than its merits.

EBP.name: Evading the Burden of Proof
EBP.explanation: This fallacy occurs when someone makes a claim but refuses to provide evidence to support it, shifting the burden of proof to others

ST.name: Strawman
ST.explanation: This involves misrepresenting someone's argument to make it easier to attack or refute than the original argument

FCD.name: Fallacy of Composition / Division
FCD.explanation: Assuming what is true of a part must be true of the whole, or vice versa.

AEM.name: Appeal to Emotion
AEM.explanation: Using emotionally charged language or imagery instead of logical reasoning.

FAUT.name: Appeal to Authority
FAUT.explanation: This fallacy is citing an authority on a topic who is not actually an expert in that field

BW.name: Bandwagon
BW.explanation: Arguing that a claim is true because many people believe it.

AT.name: Appeal to Tradition
AT.explanation: Claiming something is correct or good because it has been done for a long time.

AI.name: Appeal to Ignorance
AI.explanation: Arguing a claim is true because it has not been proven false, or vice versa.

SS.name: Slippery Slope
SS.explanation: Claiming a small first step will inevitably lead to extreme and undesirable outcomes.

RH.name: Red Herring
RH.explanation: This fallacy involves diverting attention from the real issue by introducing an irrelevant topic

BTQ.name: Begging the Question
BTQ.explanation: Assuming the truth of the conclusion within the premises of the argument.

FF.name: Formal Fallacy
FF.explanation: An error in logical structure that makes the argument invalid.

CP.name: Cherry Picking
CP.explanation: Selectively presenting evidence that supports one's argument while ignoring evidence that contradicts it

FA.name: False Analogy
FA.explanation: Making a misleading comparison between two things that are not truly comparable

HG.name: Hasty Generalization
HG.explanation: Making a generalized statement based on a small or unrepresentative sample

PH.name: Post Hoc
PH.explanation: Assuming that because one event followed another, the first event caused the second

FC.name: False Cause
FC.explanation: Mistaking correlation for causation, assuming that because two events occur together, one causes the other

VAG.name: Vagueness
VAG.explanation: Using imprecise, unclear, or ambiguous language in an argument

FD.name: False Dilemma
FD.explanation: Presenting only two options when more possibilities exist.

DPF.name: Decision Point Fallacy
DPF.explanation: Claiming no distinction exists because no precise cutoff can be identified.

EQ.name: Equivocation
EQ.explanation: Using a word in multiple senses within the same argument to mislead.

SAT.name: Setting an Arbitrary Threshold
SAT.explanation: This fallacy occurs when an arbitrary standard is set to judge a phenomenon, without considering the broader context or implications

IDV.name: Issues with Data Validity
IDV.explanation: This fallacy arises when there are concerns about the accuracy and consistency of data, which are either exaggerated or ignored to support a preconceived notion

FASN.name: Failure to Account for Statistical Nuance
FASN.group: Failure to Account for Statistical Nuance
FASN.explanation: This occurs when crucial statistical details are overlooked or simplified in an argument, leading to misleading conclusions

MOSS.name: Misrepresentation of Scientific Studies
MOSS.explanation: This involves exaggerating the significance of certain scientific findings that align with one's beliefs or outright rejecting scientific authority in favor of personal anecdotes or pseudo-science

PM.name: Priming Message
PM.explanation: Introducing biased framing early to shape how readers interpret subsequent information.

TL.name: Toxic Language
TL.explanation: Using hostile, inflammatory, or demeaning language to provoke emotional reactions.

GT.name: Groupthink Language
GT.explanation: Assigning readers to a group identity and asserting how that group thinks or should think.
